growth_thesis.claim: For retention-supported recurring growth to continue, RingCentral must limit customer turnover, seat reductions, and down-selling, because month-to-month customers can cancel without penalty and contracted customers have no obligation to renew after their initial term.
quotes: Although we have entered into long-term subscription contracts with larger customers, those customers with month to month contracts with us may terminate their subscriptions at any time without penalty or early termination charges and customers under contract may not renew.

Our customers with non-month-to-month subscription agreements have no obligation to renew their subscriptions for our service after the expiration of their initial subscription period, which is typically between one and three years, and a substantial portion of our large contracts are up for renewal every year.

We have in the past and may in the future experience lower upsell and increased downsell within our existing base as customers may slow hiring and rationalize their employee counts or lower average revenue per user.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Risk Factors.
growth_thesis.claim: For AI-led and new-product growth to continue, RingCentral must introduce and sell new solutions—including RingCX, AI Receptionist, AI Virtual Assistant, AI Conversation Expert, RingWEM, and RingCentral Events—on time and without defects while avoiding AI-driven obsolescence of core products.
quotes: However, our future success may also depend on our ability to introduce and sell new services, features, and functionality, such as RingCX, AI Receptionist, AI Virtual Assistant, AI Conversation Expert, RingWEM, and RingCentral Events that enhance or are in addition to the subscriptions we currently offer, as well as to improve usability and support and increase customer satisfaction.
There are significant risks involved in deploying AI and there can be no assurance that using AI in our platforms and products will enhance or be beneficial to our business.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.

quotes: RingCentral’s core tenets include: a) Trust: We provide a carrier-grade, cloud-based communications platform that businesses can trust with reliability, security, and privacy; b) Innovation: We have invested over $250 million in research and development in 2026 to execute through focused and strategic innovation, setting the bar in the industry for many market firsts; c) Partnerships: We have a diverse set of strategic partners, global service providers, channel partners, and third-party developers.
We devote the majority of our research and development resources to software development with growing investments in our agentic voice AI platform.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
growth_thesis.claim: For R&D-led product innovation to sustain growth, RingCentral must continue funding substantial engineering investments while achieving wide customer adoption so those investments generate a return.
quotes: Moreover, the development of new or enhanced services or applications will require substantial investment, and we must continue to invest a significant amount of resources in our research and development efforts to develop these services and applications to remain competitive.
If customers do not widely adopt any new or enhanced services and applications, we may not be able to realize a return on our investment.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A Risk Factors.
growth_thesis.claim: RingCentral uses indirect sales channels—including resellers, distributors, strategic partners, and global service providers—to broaden solution adoption and access partner customer bases, generating a substantial portion of revenues.
quotes: Our indirect sales channels help broaden the adoption of our solutions and enable us to leverage the channel to sell our services as well as access their customer bases.
A substantial portion of our revenues is derived from our network of sales agents, brokers, and resellers, which we refer to collectively as channel partners.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
growth_thesis.claim: For indirect channel growth to continue, RingCentral must maintain partner relationships without long-term commitments, prevent partners from favoring competitors, and complete its transition to a resale/wholesale channel model without system or process delays.
quotes: Our future success depends, in part on our continued ability to establish and maintain a network of channel relationships and strategic partnerships, including GSPs.
In addition, we are in the process of adjusting our channel partner go-to-market strategy, to better enable a resale/wholesale model, which requires significant changes to our systems and processes.
These system and process changes could result in longer time to implement our strategy which could have an impact on our revenue.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
growth_thesis.claim: RingCentral pursues multi-product expansion across enterprise and SMB customers and sees additional growth opportunities in international markets outside its current U.S. and Canada concentration.
quotes: We continue to look to expand our offerings in new geographies and believe that there are additional growth opportunities in international markets.
Our future success also depends in part on our ability to execute upon our multi-product strategy to sell additional subscriptions for additional and/or new functionalities to our current customers.
For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, the vast majority of our total revenues were generated in the U.S. and Canada.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Risk Factors.
